dimensions.note: The SSH private key is sensitive-marked on the string and its nullish wrapper and reaches ssh through a key file, never argv; the S3 accessKey/secretKey are sensitive and used only to sign SigV4 (no URL, header or signature reaches a record, log or error); RGW user keys and CSI client keys are generated or read into sensitive, vaulted resource fields (the user record's accessKey is sensitive-marked beside key). Known external issue swamp-club lab 3555: README examples pass secrets as vault references only and never show --json.
Methods log structured, value-free summaries (host, method, verdict); remote stderr and S3 transport detail are URL-stripped and truncated before they reach logs or errors.

Failures are typed (validate, transport, unverifiable, protected, object-leak-*, policy rollback) with bounded detail; SSH exit 255 is a typed transport error; indeterminate S3 writes are re-read and rolled back, and RESTORED is reported only after a canonical read-back.

486 unit/contract tests with scripted SSH sessions and an injected fetch (no socket), including the wipe guard's refusal matrix, SigV4 known-answer tests, workflow catalog tests (manifest vs directory, gate polarity, succeeded-only safety dependencies) and plain-object method contexts. Live end-to-end is BLOCKED: a real cluster needs at least three hosts with free whole disks and the one bare-metal test box has root RAID1 members on both disks; every live cell (77) is recorded as blocked in LOGBOOK, which is why the channel is beta.

Every ensure/apply method reads first and converges or does nothing (bootstrap no-ops on an existing cluster, placement converges to an explicit list keeping quorum, pools/fs/users adopt); delete paths are double-confirmed and re-runs are clean no-ops; maintenance enter/exit prove their effect. Residual LOW: probe-cleanup fallback after an unreadable version listing reports success after a plain DELETE.

Public cephadm/ceph CLI over SSH (pinned cephadm binary from a caller-supplied URL), Ceph RGW admin via radosgw-admin, and the RGW S3 API with SigV4; PutObjectAcl (not a second PutObject) for the leak probe; versioning is the three-state model.
SSH sessions are closed per call (optional multiplexing is opt-in); remote temp files are removed in finally paths; S3 responses are capped at 1 MiB; every wait is bounded.

Manifest @randybias/cephadm, two-sentence description, Apache-2.0, additionalFiles README.md and LICENSE.txt (LOGBOOK not packaged). Destructive methods lead with DESTRUCTIVE., read-only with READ-ONLY.; README method table regenerated from source (50 methods, 22 workflows). Fixtures are synthetic (RFC 5737, example.com/.test); leak scan, gitleaks and fixture guard pass. Clean-room provenance is logged in docs/CLEANROOM.md.

Global arguments are an empty strictObject; every method argument object is strict with grammars and bounds for hosts, devices, pool/fs/user/bucket names and URLs; strictHostKeyChecking is a required yes/no enum; bucket policy documents are parsed, validated and re-serialized from the validated structure.
34 result resources lifetime infinite with garbageCollection 10; the CSI key resource keeps 2 versions.

Host prep, bootstrap, enrol, mon/mgr/mds/osd placement, pools, CephFS, CSI users and keys, maintenance, teardown, RGW users and buckets, plus verify methods for each; every mutator is kind action (25 methods), so no verb tombstones the definition; 22 workflows gate every mutation behind a pre-check and manual approval.

wipeDiskToRaw refuses any device that backs the running or bootable system (protected-device closure over lsblk, blkid, mdstat, mdadm --examine, pvs and ZFS), and refuses when lsblk and blkid disagree; destructive teardown requires the named fsid; placement changes are judged against live quorum first.
Workflows address the instance cephadm or cephadm-<purpose>-<item> for a fan-out, and each assert reads the record from the instance that wrote it.
Every host, credential and target arrives as method arguments, so one generic definition serves any cluster; the model reads no other model's data.
First release (2026.10.17.1): no earlier version or stored data to upgrade.
